1	# Atomic model: how we classify components
2	
3	The single rule that decides whether a UI element is an **atom**, **molecule**,
4	**organism**, **template**, or **page**. It is transitive and machine-checkable (see
5	`02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs`). The contract records the tier for
6	every component at the atom, molecule, and organism level only.
7	
8	---
9	
10	## The five tiers
11	
12	| Tier | Definition (by what the component's **own template renders**) |
13	|---|---|
14	| **Atom** | Renders **no other component**: markup + CSS + tokens only. |
15	| **Molecule** | Renders **only atoms**. |
16	| **Organism** | Renders **at least one molecule**. |
17	| **Template** | Defines the **skeletal page frame**: a set of named structural regions, their arrangement, and responsive layout. No real content. Renders at least one organism. |
18	| **Page** | A **template instance** with real content applied. Defines the section arrangement within the primary content region for a specific page type. |
19	
20	> The boundary is set by what a component's template renders *itself*, recorded
21	> as `composes: [...]` in the contract. An atom has `composes: []`.
22	> Templates and pages are not recorded in the contract and are not delivered
23	> as Custom Elements. See Rule F.
24	
25	---
26	
27	## Rule A: icons are attributes, not components
28	
29	A glyph is delivered by an **attribute value** (e.g. `icon="arrow-right"`), never
30	by composing a separate Icon component. A component that accepts an icon attribute
31	composes nothing for that icon.
32	
33	- A Button with a leading icon → still an **atom** (icon is an attribute, not a composed component).
34	- Only a standalone displayed glyph is the `Icon` atom itself.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## Rule B: slot ≠ import
39	
40	A component passed **in** as slotted content does **not** change the parent's tier.
41	Only what the parent's own template renders itself counts.
42	
43	- A container that merely *holds* slotted children stays at its own tier.
44	- A Card that renders a CardHeader molecule in its own template → **organism**,
45	  regardless of what is slotted into its body.
46	
47	---
48	
49	## Rule C: Template defines structure, not content
50	
51	A template establishes the page frame and the positions of its structural regions.
52	It contains no real copy, imagery, or data. If a Figma frame contains real content,
53	it is a Page, not a Template.
54	
55	- A frame with a nav region, a grey placeholder hero, and a footer region → **Template**.
56	- The same frame with a real headline, product image, and body copy → **Page**.
57	
58	---
59	
60	## Rule D: Page is always an instance of a template
61	
62	Every page type belongs to exactly one template. Multiple page types can share the
63	same template shell. A new page type is only warranted when the section arrangement
64	within the primary content region differs materially from an existing one.
65	
66	- "About Us" and "About Us - History" sharing the same section rhythm → same page type, same template.
67	- "Offerings" with a fundamentally different section arrangement → separate page type.
68	
69	---
70	
71	## Rule E: Layout sections are not components
72	
73	Blocks and sections within the primary content region are layout instructions:
74	spacing, background colour, and container-query responsive sizing. They do not
75	receive contract entries unless they render component content themselves. Classify
76	them by structural role, not visual scale.
77	
78	---
79	
80	## Rule F: Templates and pages are not Custom Elements
81	
82	Templates and pages sit above the component delivery layer. They are
83	**spec-layer deliverables only**. They do not receive contract entries, do not
84	generate `.js` component files, and are not delivered as Custom Elements.
85	
86	The design system provides atoms, molecules, and organisms. How a developer
87	assembles those into a page frame within their stack (React layouts, Angular shell
88	components, LWC experience layers, vanilla HTML) is outside the scope of the
89	component library. A template spec communicates layout intent: the named regions,
90	which components live in each, and the responsive behaviour. Implementation is the
91	developer's decision.
92	
93	---
94	
95	## Edge tests (apply in this order)
96	
97	1. **Decorative internals are not components.** A badge dot, a toggle knob, a
98	   slider thumb: styled elements with no standalone identity. They do **not** bump
99	   the tier.
100	2. **Atom-only regions are molecules.** A top bar composing only Button + Logo →
101	   **molecule**, even though it spans the full viewport. Tier follows composition,
102	   not pixel size.
103	3. **Containers follow their template.** If a component's own template renders a
104	   molecule, it is an organism.
105	
106	---
107	
108	## Reading a Figma frame labelled as a template or page
109	
110	1. **Read structure first.** Identify the named structural regions in the frame,
111	   their vertical order, nesting depth, and responsive or breakpoint intent.
112	
113	2. **Map regions to semantic HTML.** Designers are not required to use HTML element
114	   names. The agent infers the semantic mapping from layer name and position.
115	   Common mappings:
116	
117	   | Figma layer name (examples) | Semantic element |
118	   |---|---|
119	   | Nav, Navigation, Nav Bar, Global Nav | `<nav>` |
120	   | Header, Site Header, Masthead | `<header>` |
121	   | Announcement Bar, Alert Bar, Promo Band | `<div>` or `<aside>` (above `<header>`) |
122	   | Hero, Page Hero, Banner | `<section>` (within `<main>`) |
123	   | Content Area, Main Content, Body | `<main>` |
124	   | Sidebar, Side Nav, Aside | `<aside>` |
125	   | Footer, Site Footer, Footer Links | `<footer>` |
126	
127	3. **Flag ambiguous names before assigning.** If a region name carries no functional
128	   signal (e.g. "Blue Bar", "Wide Strip"), stop and ask before assigning a semantic
129	   element.
130	
131	4. **Then read composition.** Once regions are mapped, identify which organisms,
132	   molecules, or atoms appear within each region.
133	
134	5. **Determine tier by content.** Placeholder text and grey boxes → Template.
135	   Real copy and imagery → Page. For frames with mixed content (some regions
136	   real, some placeholder), classify by the majority: if most regions carry real
137	   content, classify as Page; if most are placeholder, classify as Template. Note
138	   the ambiguity in the spec's Overview section so the designer can verify.
139	
140	6. **Note repeating sections.** Layout sections that repeat across subpages of the
141	   same type define the page type's identity. Document them in the spec as
142	   page-type structure, not as individual components.
143	
144	---
145	
146	## When you need something new
147	
148	If a component or variant is not in the contract, **STOP and flag it** as a
149	proposed contract addition. Do not invent a component outside the contract.
150	Adding it means: a new contract entry + the tier decided by these rules +
151	implementation as a Custom Element. This applies to atoms, molecules, and organisms
152	only. Templates and pages are never added to the contract.
153

# Design OS Portability Protocol

Read this during the path resolution pre-flight of any skill. Resolves Design OS paths from project config and handles missing structure gracefully.

---

## Step 1: Resolve paths

Check for `project.config.js` at the repo root.

- If found: read it. If a `paths` object is present, use those values to override the defaults below. Keys not present in `paths` fall back to Design OS defaults.
- If not found: use Design OS defaults for all paths. Note in context that this may not be an Design OS project.

**Default paths (override via `paths` in `project.config.js`):**

| Config key | Default path |
|---|---|
| `contextRoot` | `01-context` |
| `contextProject` | `01-context/project-context.md` |
| `contextDecisions` | `01-context/decisions.md` |
| `contextSummaries` | `01-context/summaries` |
| `contextDiscovery` | `01-context/discovery` |
| `contextRefsLocal` | `01-context/ref-local` |
| `contextRefsExt` | `01-context/ref-external` |
| `design` | `02-design` |
| `library` | `02-design/library` |
| `libraryTokens` | `02-design/library/tokens.md` |
| `libraryCss` | `02-design/library/common.css` |
| `libraryElements` | `02-design/library/elements` |
| `specs` | `02-design/specs` |
| `prototypes` | `02-design/prototypes` |
| `ia` | `02-design/ia` |
| `viewer` | `02-design/viewer` |
| `requirements` | `03-requirements` |
| `feedback` | `04-feedback` |
| `handover` | `05-handover` |

---

## Step 2: Check required paths

For each path marked **Required** in the calling skill's pre-flight: check whether it exists at the resolved location.

If one or more required paths are missing, stop and surface them before proceeding:

> "[skill name]: Some required paths are missing.
>
> Missing:
> - `[resolved path]`
>
> How would you like to proceed?
> (a) Create the standard Design OS folder structure for the missing paths
> (b) Point me to your existing locations (used for this session only, not saved)
> (c) Continue without them (this skill will run in limited mode, some features unavailable)
>
> You can also run `/setup` to permanently map your project structure to Design OS conventions."

Wait for the user's response before proceeding.

- **(a) Create:** create the missing folders and any required stub files at their Design OS default paths. If `project.config.js` does not exist, offer to create a minimal one.
- **(b) Redirect:** ask for each missing path one at a time. Store the custom locations in context for this session only.
- **(c) Continue:** note which features are unavailable. Proceed with what exists.

---

## Step 3: Handle optional paths

For each path marked **Optional**: check whether it exists. If missing, note it silently. Do not stop or prompt the user unless the missing path directly changes the skill's output (e.g. "No library tokens found, prototype will scaffold in greyscale mode.").

---

## Step 4: Return

All path resolution is complete. Proceed with the calling skill using resolved paths throughout. Do not use hardcoded Design OS defaults after this point if overrides were found.

# Sub-skill: Handover Index Generator

Called by `/handover` Step 3. Generates or updates `05-handover/index.md`.

---

## Step 1: Read project identity

Read `project.config.js`. Extract: `project`, `client`, `lead`, `stacks`, `wcag`, and `viewer.deployUrl` (if set).

---

## Step 2: Scan deliverables

Scan the following and collect results:

**Tokens and design library:**
- Check if `02-design/library/tokens.md` exists
- Check if `02-design/library/common.css` exists

**Components (from contract):**
- Read `project.config.js` for `componentPrefix` and `catalog.deployUrl`
- Read `02-design/library/contract/[prefix]-contract.js`
- Group entries by `atomic` tier: atom, molecule, organism
- For each entry, note: `element`, `name`, status, JS file path (`02-design/library/elements/[name]/[element].js`)
- If the contract is empty or missing, note it (components section will say "No components extracted yet")

**Specs:**
- `02-design/specs/screens/`: all `.md` files (exclude `.gitkeep`, `README.md`)
- `02-design/specs/flows/`: all `.md` files
- `02-design/specs/templates/`: all `.md` files
- For each spec file, read its `**Status:**` field. Default to `draft` if absent.
- For template specs, also read the `**Type:**` and `**Page types:**` bold metadata lines in the spec header. These are body fields (e.g. `**Type:** template`), not YAML frontmatter.
- Note: component specs live in the contract. Do not scan `02-design/specs/components/` for the index.

**Prototypes:**
- `02-design/prototypes/`: for each subfolder (exclude `_platform/`), check for `intent.md`
- From each `intent.md` extract: `stage`, `stack`, `viewer-label` (fall back to humanised folder name)
- Note the `index.html` path in the same folder (it is always `[folder]/index.html`)

**Requirements:**
- Count `.md` files in `03-requirements/epics/`, `03-requirements/features/`, `03-requirements/stories/`

**Context:**
- Check if `01-context/decisions.md` exists and is non-empty
- Check if `01-context/discovery/` contains any `.md` files

**BMAD output (conditional):**
- Check if `05-handover/bmad/` exists
- If yes, note which of the following are present: `DESIGN.md`, `EXPERIENCE.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `delivery-overview.md`

---

## Step 3: Write the index

Rewrite the body of `05-handover/index.md` using the template below. Preserve and prepend the changelog block. Fill all tables from the scanned data. Omit any row or section only where the source genuinely does not exist yet. Do not omit table headers.

```markdown
<!-- managed-by: /handover | do-not-edit -->
<!-- changelog
YYYY-MM-DD | /handover | [one-line summary of what changed]
[preserve any existing entries below this line]
Full history: GitHub → 05-handover/index.md → History
-->

# [project]: Engineering handover

**Client:** [client]
**Lead:** [lead]
**Component prefix:** `[componentPrefix]`
**Stacks:** [stacks joined by comma]
**WCAG:** [wcag]
**Last updated:** [DD MMM YYYY]
**Build Status:** [status]

> Table of contents for engineering and AI-assisted development. The whole repository is the handover. This file links to assets across every folder. Managed by `/handover`. Do not edit manually.

Called by `/handover` Step 3.5 (opt-in). Translates completed Design OS artefacts into BMAD-compatible markdown files. Output lands in `05-handover/bmad/`. Nothing in the Design OS structure is modified.

BMAD format reference: two-spine contract (`DESIGN.md` + `EXPERIENCE.md`) plus delivery support files. Compatible with `bmad-create-epics-and-stories` ingestion.

---

## Step 1: Confirm source state

Check that the following exist before proceeding. If any are missing, surface a warning and ask whether to continue without them:

- `02-design/library/tokens.md`
- `02-design/library/common.css`
- At least one file in `02-design/specs/components/` or `02-design/specs/screens/`
- `05-handover/index.md`

---

## Step 2: Create output folder

Ensure `05-handover/bmad/` exists. If not, create it.

Write a `README.md` into it:

```markdown
# BMAD Handover Output

Generated by `/handover` from Design OS design artefacts. Do not edit manually.
Re-run `/handover` and select the BMAD output option to regenerate.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| DESIGN.md | Visual identity: tokens, component definitions, design system |
| EXPERIENCE.md | Behaviour: interaction flows, state maps, routing |
| acceptance-criteria.md | QA checklist: Happy Path, Error Handling, Accessibility |
| delivery-overview.md | Inventory: all specs, components, and prototypes in this handover |

## To complete the handoff

Copy the contents of this folder into the dev team's BMAD project at:

```
{planning_artifacts}/ux-designs/[project-name]/
```

The BMAD Scrum Master agent (`bmad-create-epics-and-stories`) reads from `{planning_artifacts}/` when generating stories. If you do not know the dev team's `planning_artifacts` path, check their `_bmad/bmm/config.yaml` (it is typically `docs/planning/`).
```

---

## Step 3: Generate DESIGN.md

Source: `02-design/library/tokens.md`, `02-design/library/common.css`, all files in `02-design/specs/components/`.

Write `05-handover/bmad/DESIGN.md` using this structure:

```markdown
<!-- generated-by: /handover bmad-export | do-not-edit -->
<!-- source: 02-design/library/tokens.md, 02-design/specs/components/ -->

# DESIGN.md: Visual Identity

**Project:** [project from project.config.js]
**Generated:** [DD MMM YYYY]

---

## Design tokens

[Synthesise the full token set from tokens.md. Organise under: Colour, Typography, Spacing, Elevation/Shadow, Motion, Radius. For each token include: name, value, and CSS variable from common.css where available.]

---

## Component definitions

[For each component spec in 02-design/specs/components/, write a concise entry:]

### [Component name]

- **Variants:** [list from spec]
- **States:** [list from spec]
- **Key tokens:** [list token names used, from spec]
- **Spec:** [relative path to source spec]
```

---

## Step 4: Generate EXPERIENCE.md

Source: all files in `02-design/specs/screens/`, `02-design/specs/flows/`, and `02-design/prototypes/` (read each `intent.md`).

Write `05-handover/bmad/EXPERIENCE.md` using this structure:

```markdown
<!-- generated-by: /handover bmad-export | do-not-edit -->
<!-- source: 02-design/specs/screens/, 02-design/specs/flows/, 02-design/prototypes/ -->

# EXPERIENCE.md: Behaviour and Interaction

**Project:** [project from project.config.js]
**Generated:** [DD MMM YYYY]

---

## Screen inventory

[For each screen spec, write a concise entry:]

### [Screen name]

- **Status:** [from spec frontmatter]
- **States covered:** [loading / error / empty / populated: list which are documented in the spec]
- **Spec:** [relative path]

---

## Interaction flows

[For each flow spec and each prototype intent.md with stage: flow or stage: interaction, write an entry:]

### [Flow or prototype name]

- **Type:** [flow | interaction | animation]
- **Stack:** [from intent.md]
- **Description:** [one-sentence summary from intent.md body or flow spec]
- **Source:** [relative path to intent.md or flow spec]

---

## State map

[Scan all screen specs for documented states (loading, error, empty, populated, disabled, active, etc.). Produce a consolidated table:]

| Screen | Loading | Error | Empty | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [name] | [yes/no/partial] | [yes/no/partial] | [yes/no/partial] | [any gap or caveat] |
```

---

## Step 5: Generate acceptance-criteria.md

Source: all spec files in `02-design/specs/components/` and `02-design/specs/screens/`. Extract any section headed `Acceptance criteria`, `Accessibility`, or `QA` from each.

Write `05-handover/bmad/acceptance-criteria.md` using this structure:

```markdown
<!-- generated-by: /handover bmad-export | do-not-edit -->
<!-- source: 02-design/specs/components/, 02-design/specs/screens/ -->

# Acceptance Criteria

**Project:** [project from project.config.js]
**Generated:** [DD MMM YYYY]

> Structured for BMAD QA agent ingestion. Organised by category. Each item references its source spec.

---

## Happy path

- [ ] [criterion] ([source spec: relative path])

---

## Error handling

- [ ] [criterion] ([source spec: relative path])

---

## Accessibility

- [ ] [criterion] ([source spec: relative path])

---

## Responsive behaviour

- [ ] [criterion] ([source spec: relative path])
```

If a spec has no acceptance criteria section, skip it silently. Do not generate placeholder rows.

---

## Step 6: Generate delivery-overview.md

Source: `05-handover/index.md` (already written by the index generator). Reformat as a BMAD delivery overview rather than duplicating the full Design OS index.

Write `05-handover/bmad/delivery-overview.md` using this structure:

```markdown
<!-- generated-by: /handover bmad-export | do-not-edit -->
<!-- source: 05-handover/index.md -->

# Delivery Overview

**Project:** [project]
**Client:** [client]
**Lead:** [lead]
**Stacks:** [stacks]
**WCAG:** [wcag]
**Generated:** [DD MMM YYYY]

> Entry point for BMAD agent ingestion. All paths are relative to repo root.
> Full Design OS handover index: [05-handover/index.md](../index.md)

---

## Design system

| Artefact | Path |
|---|---|
| Tokens | 02-design/library/tokens.md |
| CSS variables | 02-design/library/common.css |
| BMAD DESIGN.md | 05-handover/bmad/DESIGN.md |

---

## Component inventory

| Component | Spec | BMAD entry |
|---|---|---|
| [name] | [relative link] | DESIGN.md#[component-name] |

---

## Screen inventory

| Screen | Spec | Status |
|---|---|---|
| [name] | [relative link] | [status] |

---

## Interaction and flows

| Name | Type | Source |
|---|---|---|
| [name] | [flow/interaction/animation] | [relative link] |

---

## BMAD artefacts in this package

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) | Visual identity and component definitions |
| [EXPERIENCE.md](EXPERIENCE.md) | Behaviour, states, interaction flows |
| [acceptance-criteria.md](acceptance-criteria.md) | QA checklist |
| [delivery-overview.md](delivery-overview.md) | This file |
```

---

## Step 7: Report

Output a brief summary:

- DESIGN.md: [n] tokens, [n] components
- EXPERIENCE.md: [n] screens, [n] flows, [n] states documented
- acceptance-criteria.md: [n] criteria extracted from [n] specs
- delivery-overview.md: written
- Any specs with no acceptance criteria (skipped silently, but count here)
- Output location: `05-handover/bmad/`

Note the folder slug and type. 56 57 ### Detect current prototype styling approach 58 59 The build tech (`prototypeStack` from config) is fixed project-wide. Detect the token source and styling approach used across existing prototypes. 60 61 For each existing prototype found: 62 1. Read its `index.html`. Check what CSS files are linked: `common.css` (library tokens), a different external CSS file or URL, or neither. 63 2. Read its `assets/styles.css`. If `prototypeStack` is `react-cdn`: check `index.html` for Tailwind CDN script tag. 65 66 Determine the current approach across all existing prototypes: 67 - **Library tokens**: links `common.css`, uses `var(--token-*)` 68 - **External token set**: links a CSS file other than `common.css`, uses that source's variable names 69 - **Self-contained**: no external CSS link, custom properties defined locally in `assets/styles.css` 70 - **Tailwind utility classes**: Tailwind CDN script present (note: temporary) 71 - **Greyscale / wireframe**: hardcoded neutral values only (e.g. `#f5f5f5`, `#333`, `#999`) 72 - **Mixed**: inconsistent across prototypes, note which ones differ 73 74 ### Read project context 75 76 Read `01-context/project-context.md` and `01-context/decisions.md` if they exist. Note any baseline / current-state context, constraints, and business rules that are relevant to prototyping. These inform the grill and the scaffold. 77 78 --- 79 80 ## Phase 2: Grill 81 82 Write a memory entry: "Skill /start-prototype started [today's date], incomplete." 83 84 Open with a one-line scan summary before the questions. For example: 85 > "Library: [no tokens / partial tokens / X colour + Y spacing tokens]. [N] components. Build: [React CDN / Vanilla] (project default). [N] existing prototypes. Token source in use: [library tokens / external / self-contained / Tailwind CDN / greyscale / mixed]." 86 87 Then ask the questions in order, one per message. Wait for each answer before asking the next. 88 89 --- 90 91 **Question 1: Fidelity.** 92 93 "What fidelity is this prototype? Wireframe (layout and structure only, greyscale), mid-fidelity (real layout and content, some token colours), or high-fidelity (full library tokens, real content, production-quality visuals)?" 94 95 This determines the scaffold comment and the note in `intent.md`. 96 97 --- 98 99 **Question 2: Continuation or new?** 100 101 Show the list of existing prototypes with their one-line intent summaries: 102 103 > "Existing prototypes:" 104 > 1. `interactions/card-expand`: demonstrates the card expanding on tap to reveal detail content 105 > 2. `flows/onboarding-flow`: shows the four-step onboarding sequence with progress indicator 106 > [etc.] 107 > 108 > "Is this prototype a continuation of one of these, or is it new?" 109 110 If yes (continuation): 111 - Ask which one: "Which prototype is this continuing from?" 112 - Silently read the selected prototype's `intent.md` and `assets/styles.css` 113 - Pre-fill Q3 and remaining questions with context from that prototype (name, spec, components, token candidates already in use) 114 - Present each pre-filled answer as a default: "[Answer carried from [slug]]. Change this?" 115 116 Also offer to open the selected prototype in the browser: "Want me to open [slug] in the browser first so you can see it?" 117 If yes: run `open 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` 118 119 If no (new): continue with Q3 blank. 120 121 --- 122 123 **Question 3: What are you prototyping?** 124 125 Only ask if new. If continuation, present pre-filled name from the selected prototype as a default to confirm or change. 126 127 "What are you prototyping? One sentence: name and brief description." 128 129 --- 130 131 **Question 4: What can Figma NOT show here?** 132 133 "What does this prototype need to communicate that Figma can't? For example: state transitions, gesture responses, multi-step flows, timing-dependent animations, conditional logic, form validation feedback, responsive layout behaviour, structural regions reflowing across viewport sizes, navigation patterns changing between breakpoints." 134 135 This is the intent statement. It goes into `intent.md` and justifies why this prototype exists. 136 137 --- 138 139 **Question 5: Prototype type.** 140 141 "What type of prototype is this? 142 - `interactions`: component state changes, hover/tap/press behaviours, micro-interactions 143 - `flows`: navigation sequences, user journeys, screen-to-screen transitions 144 - `tokens`: visual reference for colours, typography, spacing, motion values 145 - `animations`: standalone animation or motion demos 146 - `templates`: page-level HTML shell demonstrating structural regions, component placement, and responsive layout behaviour. Contains real or placeholder components. Required for any template or page spec. 147 148 Note: the folder type is `templates` (plural) but the value written to the `stage` field in `intent.md` is `template` (singular). The scaffold handles this automatically." 149 150 --- 151 152 **Question 6: Folder slug.** 153 154 "What's the folder slug? Kebab-case, becomes the folder name. Existing: [list]. Examples: `card-expand`, `onboarding-flow`, `colour-palette`." 155 156 Show existing prototype folders so they can match naming conventions. 157 158 --- 159 160 **Question 7: Which spec does this feed into?** 161 162 "Which spec does this prototype feed into? [show list of available spec files from scan, or 'No specs found yet.']" 163 164 If no specs exist, they can enter "TBD". The field will be left as a placeholder in `intent.md`. 165 166 --- 167 168 **Question 8: [Conditional] Design target.** 169 170 "What platform or device is this prototype designed for? iOS, Android, or web browser. This sets the device frame in the viewer and determines whether platform reference styles (HIG for iOS, Material Design for Android) are loaded alongside your tokens." 171 172 Only ask this if design target mode is `multi-mobile`, `mixed`, or `unknown` (see Phase 1). 173 If `mobile-only`: state which target was auto-detected and ask them to confirm. 174 If `web-only`: skip this question entirely. 175 If type is `templates`: skip this question regardless of mode. Template prototypes are always web. Set design target to `web` automatically and note it in the Phase 3 report. 176 177 Valid values: `ios`, `android`, `web`, `react`, `angular`, `lwc` 178 179 --- 180 181 **Question 9: Token source.** 182 183 "Where are your design tokens coming from? 184 (a) Library tokens: `02-design/library/common.css`. Library is currently [populated / partial / empty]. Impact: prototype depends on this repo. Token changes in the library immediately affect all prototypes using it. 185 (b) External token set: a different CSS file or URL. Impact: prototype depends on that source. Confirm it is stable and accessible before sharing. 186 (c) Self-contained: all values defined inside `assets/styles.css`. Fully portable, no external dependency. Impact: tokens are isolated and will not be promoted to the library unless you mark and extract them manually. 187 (d) Tailwind CDN: utility classes, no token variables. Impact: temporary, must be replaced before handover. 188 (e) Greyscale / wireframe: neutral values only. Impact: layout exploration only, not suitable for visual review." 189 190 If (a): follow up immediately: "Which tokens from the library do you plan to reference? [show scanned token list]" 191 If (a) and library is empty: "No tokens are in the library yet. You can still choose library mode and define values in `assets/styles.css` marked `/* token candidate */`. Promote them via `/extract` later." 192 If (b): ask for the path or URL to the external CSS file before continuing. 193 194 Record the confirmed choice as the token source. Used in the scaffold and `intent.md`. 195 196 --- 197 198 **Question 10: Components.** 199 200 "The library has [N] extracted components: [list names]. Are any of these relevant to this prototype?" 201 202 If no components in library: "No components have been extracted to the library yet. Build the prototype first, then run `/extract` to add them." 203 204 --- 205 206 **Question 11: [Conditional] Baseline reference.** 207 208 Only ask this if `01-context/project-context.md` contains baseline context or `01-context/ref-local/baseline/` has files. If so: 209 210 "I found baseline context: [one-line summary from project-context]. Should this prototype reference or compare against the current state, or is it a net-new design?" 211 212 If no baseline exists: skip this question. 213 214 --- 215 216 ## Phase 3: Report and scaffold 217 218 ### Report 219 220 After receiving answers, present a one-screen summary before scaffolding: 221 222 ``` 223 Prototype: [name/slug] 224 Type: [type] 225 Stack: [stack] 226 Fidelity: [wireframe / mid-fi / hi-fi] 227 Token source: [library / external: [source] / self-contained / Tailwind CDN (temporary) / greyscale] 228 Stage: [interaction | flow | tokens | animation | template] 229 Spec: [spec path or TBD] 230 Baseline: [yes, referencing [source] / no] 231 232 Assets available 233 Tokens: [populated / partial / empty, and brief note] 234 Components: [list relevant ones, or none] 235 236 Gaps 237 [List any: empty library, missing spec, platform styles not found, CDN in use, etc.] 238 239 Platform guardrail 240 [If mobile: "05-handover/platform/[stack]/README.md exists. Review before building."] 241 [If mobile + _platform CSS exists: "02-design/prototypes/_platform/[stack].css will be linked."] 242 [If mobile + _platform CSS missing: "WARNING: 02-design/prototypes/_platform/[stack].css not found. Run /setup-local or check the repo."] 243 244 Scaffold 245 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html 246 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/styles.css 247 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md 248 ``` 249 250 Ask: "Scaffold this prototype?" 251 252 --- 253 254 ### Scaffold 255 256 On confirmation, create the following files. 257 258 #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` 259 260 **If type is `templates`:** Scaffold a semantic page shell directly using the structure below. Do not use the standard `react-cdn.html` or `vanilla.html` templates. They are component sandboxes, not page frames. 261 262 ```html 263 264 265 266 267 268 [Template Name]: Template Demo 269 270 271 272 273 274 275 276 277
278 279
[ Header region placeholder ]
280
281 282
283 284
[ Main content region placeholder ]
285
286 287
288 289
[ Footer region placeholder ]
290
291 292 293 294 ``` 295 296 Add any additional named regions (announcement bar, sidebar, etc.) between the standard regions as needed. Each region gets a `.region-[name]` class and a `data-region` attribute matching the spec's region name. Apply the same conditional CSS link logic as below. 297 298 **For all other types:** Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/react-cdn.html` or `templates/vanilla.html` (based on `prototypeStack` from config). Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. Apply conditional include lines: 299 - Include `common.css` link only if token source is library (a). 300 - Include the external CSS link only if token source is external (b). Use the confirmed path or URL. 301 - Omit any token CSS link if token source is self-contained (c), Tailwind (d), or greyscale (e). 302 - Include the `_platform` stylesheet only if design target is `ios` or `android`. 303 - Include the Tailwind CDN script only if the designer confirmed Tailwind (d). 304 - React CDN scripts are always included when `prototypeStack` is `react-cdn`. 305 306 Path notes (always correct, do not change): 307 - `../../../library/common.css`: 3 levels up from `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/`. 308 - `../../_platform/[target].css`: 2 levels up from the prototype folder. 309 310 #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/styles.css` 311 312 Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/styles.css`. Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. 313 314 #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md` 315 316 Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/intent.md`. Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. 317 318 --- 319 320 ### After scaffolding 321 322 Tell the designer: 323 324 1. Open `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` in a browser. It will render immediately. 325 2. [If react-cdn]: Build your UI as React components inside the `` in the ``. 340 341 Update the memory entry to: "Skill /start-prototype completed [today's date], slug: [slug]." 342

If continuation, present pre-filled name from the selected prototype as a default to confirm or change. "What are you prototyping? One sentence: name and brief description." --- **Question 4: What can Figma NOT show here?** "What does this prototype need to communicate that Figma can't? For example: state transitions, gesture responses, multi-step flows, timing-dependent animations, conditional logic, form validation feedback, responsive layout behaviour, structural regions reflowing across viewport sizes, navigation patterns changing between breakpoints." This is the intent statement. It goes into `intent.md` and justifies why this prototype exists. --- **Question 5: Prototype type.** "What type of prototype is this? - `interactions`: component state changes, hover/tap/press behaviours, micro-interactions - `flows`: navigation sequences, user journeys, screen-to-screen transitions - `tokens`: visual reference for colours, typography, spacing, motion values - `animations`: standalone animation or motion demos - `templates`: page-level HTML shell demonstrating structural regions, component placement, and responsive layout behaviour. Contains real or placeholder components. Required for any template or page spec. Note: the folder type is `templates` (plural) but the value written to the `stage` field in `intent.md` is `template` (singular). Show existing prototype folders so they can match naming conventions. --- **Question 7: Which spec does this feed into?** "Which spec does this prototype feed into? The field will be left as a placeholder in `intent.md`. --- **Question 8: [Conditional] Design target.** "What platform or device is this prototype designed for? iOS, Android, or web browser. Only ask this if design target mode is `multi-mobile`, `mixed`, or `unknown` (see Phase 1). If `mobile-only`: state which target was auto-detected and ask them to confirm. If `web-only`: skip this question entirely. If type is `templates`: skip this question regardless of mode. Template prototypes are always web. Set design target to `web` automatically and note it in the Phase 3 report. Valid values: `ios`, `android`, `web`, `react`, `angular`, `lwc` --- **Question 9: Token source.** "Where are your design tokens coming from? (a) Library tokens: `02-design/library/common.css`. Library is currently [populated / partial / empty]. Impact: prototype depends on this repo. Token changes in the library immediately affect all prototypes using it. (b) External token set: a different CSS file or URL. Impact: prototype depends on that source. Confirm it is stable and accessible before sharing. (c) Self-contained: all values defined inside `assets/styles.css`. Fully portable, no external dependency. Impact: tokens are isolated and will not be promoted to the library unless you mark and extract them manually. (d) Tailwind CDN: utility classes, no token variables. Impact: temporary, must be replaced before handover. (e) Greyscale / wireframe: neutral values only. Impact: layout exploration only, not suitable for visual review." If (a): follow up immediately: "Which tokens from the library do you plan to reference? [show scanned token list]" If (a) and library is empty: "No tokens are in the library yet. You can still choose library mode and define values in `assets/styles.css` marked `/* token candidate */`. Promote them via `/extract` later." If (b): ask for the path or URL to the external CSS file before continuing. Record the confirmed choice as the token source. Used in the scaffold and `intent.md`. --- **Question 10: Components.** "The library has [N] extracted components: [list names]. Are any of these relevant to this prototype?" If no components in library: "No components have been extracted to the library yet. Build the prototype first, then run `/extract` to add them." --- **Question 11: [Conditional] Baseline reference.** Only ask this if `01-context/project-context.md` contains baseline context or `01-context/ref-local/baseline/` has files. If so: "I found baseline context: [one-line summary from project-context]. Should this prototype reference or compare against the current state, or is it a net-new design?" If no baseline exists: skip this question. --- ## Phase 3: Report and scaffold ### Report After receiving answers, present a one-screen summary before scaffolding: ``` Prototype: [name/slug] Type: [type] Stack: [stack] Fidelity: [wireframe / mid-fi / hi-fi] Token source: [library / external: [source] / self-contained / Tailwind CDN (temporary) / greyscale] Stage: [interaction | flow | tokens | animation | template] Spec: [spec path or TBD] Baseline: [yes, referencing [source] / no] Assets available Tokens: [populated / partial / empty, and brief note] Components: [list relevant ones, or none] Gaps [List any: empty library, missing spec, platform styles not found, CDN in use, etc.] Platform guardrail [If mobile: "05-handover/platform/[stack]/README.md exists. Review before building."] [If mobile + _platform CSS exists: "02-design/prototypes/_platform/[stack].css will be linked."] [If mobile + _platform CSS missing: "WARNING: 02-design/prototypes/_platform/[stack].css not found. Run /setup-local or check the repo."] Scaffold 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/styles.css 02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md ``` Ask: "Scaffold this prototype?" --- ### Scaffold On confirmation, create the following files. #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/index.html` **If type is `templates`:** Scaffold a semantic page shell directly using the structure below. Do not use the standard `react-cdn.html` or `vanilla.html` templates. They are component sandboxes, not page frames. ```html [Template Name]: Template Demo
[ Header region placeholder ]
[ Main content region placeholder ]
[ Footer region placeholder ]
``` Add any additional named regions (announcement bar, sidebar, etc.) between the standard regions as needed. Each region gets a `.region-[name]` class and a `data-region` attribute matching the spec's region name. Apply the same conditional CSS link logic as below. **For all other types:** Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/react-cdn.html` or `templates/vanilla.html` (based on `prototypeStack` from config). Path notes (always correct, do not change): - `../../../library/common.css`: 3 levels up from `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/`. - `../../_platform/[target].css`: 2 levels up from the prototype folder. #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/assets/styles.css` Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/styles.css`. Fill in all `[bracketed]` placeholders from the grill answers. #### `02-design/prototypes/[type]/[slug]/intent.md` Read `.claude/skills/start-prototype/templates/intent.md`. # Component contract

The contract is the single source of truth for the component API. Every component
that exists (its name, tier, attributes, slots, composition, and accessibility
requirements) is recorded here. If it is not in the contract, it does not exist.

---

## What is in this folder

| File | What it is |
|---|---|
| `[prefix]-contract.js` | The contract: an array of component definitions. Generated and maintained by `/extract`. |
| `validate.mjs` | Checks the atomic model rules against the contract. Run before any handover. |

---

## How to read a contract entry

```js
{
  name:      "Button",          // PascalCase component name
  prefix:    "ds",              // tag namespace (from project.config.js)
  element:   "ds-button",       // the custom element tag
  atomic:    "atom",            // atom | molecule | organism
  composes:  [],                // elements this component renders in its own template
  attributes: [
    { name: "variant", type: "enum",    values: ["primary","secondary","ghost"], default: "primary" },
    { name: "size",    type: "enum",    values: ["sm","md","lg"],                default: "md" },
    { name: "disabled",type: "boolean",                                          default: false },
  ],
  slots: [
    { name: "default", description: "Button label text" },
  ],
  a11y:      "role=button, aria-disabled when disabled, keyboard: Enter and Space activate",
  status:    "final",           // draft | in-review | final
  extracted: "2026-07-07",
}
```

**`atomic`**: the component's tier, determined by what it renders in its own template:
- `atom`: renders no other component. `composes: []`.
- `molecule`: renders only atoms.
- `organism`: renders at least one molecule.

`template` and `page` are not valid contract tiers. They are layout-layer deliverables, not Custom Elements. See atomic model Rule F in `.claude/skills/_shared/atomic-model.md`.

**`composes`**: what the component's own template renders. Slotted children are not listed here (see atomic model Rule B). This determines the tier and build order: build atoms first, then molecules, then organisms.

**`attributes`**: the component's public API. These map directly to `observedAttributes` in the Custom Element. Types:
- `enum`: a fixed set of values. Use the `default` if none is passed or the value is unrecognised.
- `boolean`: present = true, absent = false.
- `string`: freeform content.

**`slots`**: named `"default"` is the element's child content. Named slots use `slot="[name]"` on a child element.

---

## How to implement a component

1. Read the contract entry for your component.
2. Build one Custom Element per entry. The `element` value is the tag to register.
3. `composes` → your imports. Build those components first.
4. `attributes` → your `observedAttributes` array and prop defaults.
5. `slots` → your shadow DOM slot elements.
6. `a11y` → bake in. Assert in tests.
7. All styles reference CSS custom properties from `02-design/library/common.css`.
   No hardcoded values.

## Definition of done (per component)

- One Custom Element matching the contract API
- All `observedAttributes` match the contract `attributes` list
- All slots match the contract `slots` list
- `composes` matches what the template actually renders
- No props or imports beyond the contract entry
- Light and dark themes verified
- `node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` passes with no violations

---

## Adding a new component

If a design needs a component not in the contract, **stop and flag it** as a proposed
addition. Do not invent a component, attribute, or token outside the contract. Raising
it means agreeing on the API, classifying the tier, extracting it via `/extract`, and
adding the entry here.

---

## Running the validator

```sh
node 02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs
```

Checks contract integrity and scans all `demo.html` files for unknown element tags.
Exit 0 = clean. Exit 1 = violations listed.

content.text:
I have all the evidence I need. Here is the audit.

---

# Workflow-as-Designed Audit: Process Control Gaps in the DDP Design OS Pipeline

Scope: the skill definitions under `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/Zimmermann-Handover/.claude/skills/`. All line citations are within that tree unless noted. I confirmed each process gap against the actual output artifacts (`02-design/library/common.css`, `02-design/library/elements/*/*.js`, the `zimm-contract.js`, and `05-handover/index.md`) to verify the downstream symptom is real, not hypothetical.

Verified baseline facts used throughout: contract holds 27 components (14 atoms / 10 molecules / 3 organisms), 26 `draft` + 1 `placeholder`, **zero `final`**; only 16 of 27 components have a spec file; `common.css` contains 54 hardcoded `px` values, a fully static px type scale, **zero** `clamp()`/`rem`/fluid tokens, and 2 `@media` rules; 18 of 27 component JS files re-declare `font-family`; `validate.mjs` exits green regardless.

---

## Finding 1 - The extraction skills contain no responsive-capture instruction whatsoever. Fixed px is the guaranteed default.
**Severity: Critical** (root cause of flagged problems #1 "absolute px" and #2 "desktop-first")

Evidence:
- `extract/library.md:150` - component extraction reads only: *"Read the component's structure, variants, states, and style values via Figma MCP."* No capture of Figma auto-layout resize behaviour (hug/fill/fixed), constraints, or min/max.
- `extract/specs.md:234-235` - the Layout section instruction is *"[Frame dimensions, padding, gap, auto-layout direction. Record exact values.]"* "Record exact values" actively directs the agent to freeze pixel measurements.
- A repo-wide grep proves the absence: `mobile-first` / `desktop-first` = **0 hits** across all skills; `clamp(` / `rem` / `fluid` / `vw` = the only hit is `_shared/authoring.md:17`, itself a hardcoded `max-width: 640px` example.
- A required "Responsive behaviour" spec section exists **only** in the template/page format (`extract/specs.md:295-296`). The component and screen spec formats (`extract/specs.md:210-245`) have no responsive section at all.

Process gap: The pipeline never instructs the agent to (a) read Figma resizing constraints, (b) emit fluid units, or (c) target a viewport direction. Responsive intent present in Figma auto-layout is discarded at read time, then "Record exact values" locks in px at write time. Whether output lands mobile-first or desktop-first is left entirely to chance.

Downstream symptom: `common.css` and every component ship fixed px (54 px literals, `--zimm-font-size-md: 24px`, `--zimm-scale-*` all px); components/screens carry no documented breakpoint behaviour. Exactly the "absolute px, desktop-first" the engineers flagged.

Fix: Add a mandatory "Step: capture responsive behaviour" to `extract/library.md` Step 2a and `extract/specs.md` Path A Step 1: record each frame's Figma resizing (hug/fill/fixed), constraints, and min/max width. Add a **required** "Responsive behaviour" section to the component and screen spec templates. Add a project-config field `layoutStrategy: mobile-first` and a token-authoring rule in `library.md` Step 1c requiring a fluid type/space strategy (rem base, `clamp()` for type ramps, breakpoint tokens) rather than raw px. Change `specs.md:235` from "Record exact values" to "Record values and their resize behaviour; express fixed-only dimensions as such."

---

## Finding 2 - /handover has no quality gate. "Ready for Build" is an unverified question, and validate.mjs green-lights an incomplete repo.
**Severity: Critical** (directly answers eval area #6)

Evidence:
- `handover/SKILL.md:42-53` - the entire pass is: run 3 extractions, then "Generate handover index." No coverage/verification step exists between extraction and index.
- `handover/index-generator.md:230-237` (Step 4) - build status is a pure prompt: *"Is this a sprint-end snapshot... or is design complete and this repo is ready for engineering build?"* then *"Write their answer as the `**Build Status:**` field."* Nothing is checked before the answer is accepted.
- `handover/index-generator.md:34` - *"Note: component specs live in the contract. Do not scan `02-design/specs/components/` for the index."* The readiness document is structurally blind to component specs, so the 11 missing ones are invisible.
- `02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs` only checks: valid tier (line 44), composition rules (lines 69-82), and that demo.html tags resolve to contract entries (lines 114-118). It checks **nothing** about spec existence, a11y content, hardcoded values, responsive units, platform-layer population, or token drift. Its success string (line 140) is *"Atomic model valid"* - but `README.md:78` and `_shared/authoring.md:121` present passing validate.mjs as the definition of done, implying far broader coverage than it has.
- `handover/bmad-export.md:184` - *"If a spec has no acceptance criteria section, skip it silently. Do not generate placeholder rows."* QA criteria can be silently empty.

Process gap: There is no gate asserting every contract component has a spec, every spec's platform layer is intentionally handled, links resolve, a11y is present, or run/build docs exist. `validate.mjs` gives false confidence: I ran it - it prints green while 11 specs are missing, `button.js` contains hardcoded px, platform layers are empty, and 26/27 components are still `draft`.

Downstream symptom: A designer can answer "Ready for Build" and the repo will assert readiness with 11 undocumented components, unconfirmed measurements, and no engineer-facing setup docs - precisely the "declared done but wasn't" condition the handover exposed.

Fix: Insert a "Step 2.5: Readiness gate" in `handover/SKILL.md` that fails loudly and lists: (1) contract components with no spec file, (2) specs still `draft` at handover, (3) specs whose Source is a screenshot/PDF/description (see Finding 4), (4) empty required sections, (5) broken relative links. Gate the "Ready for Build" option in `index-generator.md` Step 4 behind this check passing - block the status, don't just record the answer. Expand `validate.mjs` to check spec-per-component and non-empty a11y, and rename its success message to "Atomic model valid (integrity only - not a coverage or a11y check)."

---

## Finding 3 - React is a declared target stack, but the pipeline emits only vanilla Custom Elements with a string-only attribute API and explicitly declares React integration out of scope.
**Severity: Critical** (directly answers eval area #7)

Evidence:
- `project.config.js:21` - `stacks: ["web", "react"]`.
- `_shared/authoring.md:115` - *"Do not use a framework-specific pattern (JSX, directives, decorators). Custom Elements only."*
- `extract/library.md:189` - output is *"A vanilla Custom Element"*; the contract API (`extract/library.md:308-315`, `contract/README.md:26-38`) supports only `enum` / `boolean` / `string` **attributes**. There is no `properties` (non-string props) and no `events` field. Grep for `dispatchEvent` / `CustomEvent` in `extract/` + `_shared/` = 0 hits: the pipeline never specifies a component's event/output interface.
- `_shared/atomic-model.md:87` and `extract/specs.md:317` both punt: *"How a developer assembles those into a page frame within their stack (React layouts...) is outside the scope of the component library."*

Process gap: Nothing in the pipeline produces React-consumable output or even documents the property/event contract a React wrapper would need. Web-component/React interop (non-string props, custom-event binding) is exactly where hand-off breaks, and the skills declare it out of scope while listing React as a target.

Downstream symptom: The React team receives 27 vanilla elements whose only interface is HTML string attributes, no typed props, no events - forcing them to rebuild or hand-wrap every component. This is a large part of why "the workflow was weak" for the actual engineering stack.

Fix: Add `events: [{name, detail, when}]` and `properties` to the contract schema in `extract/library.md` and `contract/README.md`, and require Step 2a to extract interactive outputs as events. Add a stack-conditional output to `library.md`: when `stacks` includes `react`, generate a thin React wrapper (or a `.d.ts` + `@lit/react`-style binding doc) per component, or at minimum a per-component "React usage" block documenting props/events. Remove the "out of scope" language or replace it with a concrete React layout-assembly guide in `05-handover/platform/web/`.

---

## Finding 4 - Figma is not required, provenance is not mandatory, MCP connectivity is never verified, and screenshot-sourcing is not flagged as a quality risk downstream.
**Severity: High** (root cause of flagged problem #4; answers eval area #1)

Evidence:
- `extract/SKILL.md:46-54` - the router accepts Storybook URLs, live sites, images (`.png/.jpg`), PDFs, and plain written descriptions as first-class spec sources, all routing to `specs.md` Path C/D. No source tier is marked lower-fidelity in the routing itself.
- `extract/SKILL.md:34` - *"For Figma URLs, use the Figma MCP to read the frame structure"* - assumes the MCP is connected; no skill verifies the Figma MCP is available/authenticated before claiming a Figma extraction. Contrast `capture-feedback/SKILL.md:9-10`, which does check for a token. `setup-local/SKILL.md:16` even tells users *"no token is needed for day-to-day use,"* so there is no credential checkpoint anywhere on the extraction path.
- `extract/specs.md:127-129` - Path C adds an `[estimated]` note to the spec body, but this is the only trace. There is no structured provenance field. Node-ID capture (`extract/specs.md:67`) is Figma-only and lives in the spec body, not in a machine-readable header.
- `handover/index-generator.md:144-170` - the index scans only a `**Status:**` field (draft/in-review/final). There is no "source fidelity" column, and component specs are not scanned at all (Finding 2). A screenshot-sourced, estimated-measurement spec is indistinguishable from a Figma-sourced one at the handover level.

Process gap: The pipeline treats a phone photo of a whiteboard and a live Figma frame as interchangeable spec inputs, never confirms it actually read Figma, and lets the "these numbers are guessed" warning die in the spec body instead of propagating to the readiness surface.

Downstream symptom: The team built from attached screenshots and the system recorded it as normal progress; unconfirmed measurements flowed to "done" with no gate. Exactly the weak-provenance failure reported.

Fix: Add a mandatory machine-readable `**Source-fidelity:**` header field (`figma` | `screenshot` | `pdf` | `description`) written by every `specs.md` path and by `library.md` Step 3b. Add a pre-flight to `extract/library.md`/`specs.md` Path A that verifies the Figma MCP responds before claiming a Figma read; if it does not, stop and surface it rather than silently falling back to a screenshot. Have `index-generator.md` add a Fidelity column and have the Finding-2 readiness gate refuse "Ready for Build" while any spec is non-`figma` fidelity or contains `[estimated]` values.

---

## Finding 5 - The skills mandate Shadow DOM encapsulation and a global common.css "referenced by all components" simultaneously, without ever reconciling that global class/element styles do not cross the shadow boundary. This forces the duplicated type layer.
**Severity: High** (root cause of flagged problem #3 "monolithic / duplicated styles"; answers eval area #4)

Evidence:
- `extract/library.md:199` + `:233` - every component `this.attachShadow({ mode: 'open' })` with the rule *"Shadow DOM for full encapsulation."*
- `_shared/authoring.md:51` - *"All visual values... come from CSS custom properties defined in `02-design/library/common.css`,"* and `index-generator.md:98` describes common.css as *"Token vars + component base styles. Reference in all component CSS."*
- Technical reality the skills never state: custom properties (`--zimm-*`) do inherit into shadow roots (so `var()` works), but **class selectors, element base styles, and utility rules in common.css do not penetrate shadow DOM.** So the "component base styles" in common.css are dead for every library element, and typography/layout must be re-declared inside each component's own `<style>`.
- Verified symptom: 18 of 27 component JS files re-declare `font-family`; `common.css` header advertises "component base styles" that no shadow-DOM element can consume.

Process gap: No skill addresses the shadow-DOM/global-CSS boundary. `_shared/authoring.md` gives no shared-style mechanism (no constructable stylesheet, no shared shadow style module, no `@import` guidance), so the only path the agent has is to copy type/base rules into every component - producing the "monolithic-feeling," duplicated styling.

Downstream symptom: A duplicated type layer across ~2/3 of components and a global CSS file whose non-token content is unreachable - the styling architecture the engineers called monolithic/duplicated.

Fix: Add a "Shadow DOM styling" section to `_shared/authoring.md` stating explicitly that only custom properties cross the boundary, and prescribe one shared mechanism (e.g. a `common-shadow.css` imported via a constructable `CSSStyleSheet` / `adoptedStyleSheets`, or a shared base-style template literal each component spreads in). Stop advertising "component base styles" in common.css (`index-generator.md:98`) unless those styles are token-only. Add a validator check flagging repeated `font-family`/base declarations across elements.

---

## Finding 6 - The "no hardcoded values" rule has no enforcement. The only check is a soft prompt the agent can pass over, and it demonstrably did.
**Severity: High** (compounds problem #1; answers eval areas #2/#3)

Evidence:
- `_shared/authoring.md:53` - *"Never hardcode a hex value, pixel value, or font name inside a component"*; `extract/library.md:232` repeats *"No hardcoded hex, pixel, or font values."*
- `extract/library.md:374-378` (Step 5) is the only check, and it is advisory: *"Scan... for any hardcoded values... Flag as: 'These values were extracted as hardcoded values... Convert any to named tokens?'"* It asks; it does not block, and `validate.mjs` never checks for literals.
- Verified symptom: shipped `02-design/library/elements/button/zimm-button.js` contains `padding: 8px`, `width: 20px`, `height: 20px`, `outline: 1px`, `border-radius: 2px`, `opacity: 0.6`, `opacity: 0.4` - straight through the "prohibition." Even the token file leaks a hardcoded alias: `common.css` `--zimm-color-text-inverse-grey: #969696` instead of `var(--zimm-color-grey-300)`.

Process gap: A prohibition with no gate is a suggestion. The soft Step 5 prompt is skippable and was skipped.

Fix: Add a hardcoded-literal scan to `validate.mjs` (fail on hex/px/font literals inside element `<style>` blocks, allowlisting structural zeros/1px hairlines if desired) and wire it into the Finding-2 handover gate. Change `extract/library.md` Step 5 from "ask to convert" to "block completion until each literal is tokenised or explicitly waived with a reason."

---

## Finding 7 - Accessibility is optional and freeform across the pipeline despite a WCAG AA target; the validator ignores it entirely.
**Severity: High** (directly answers eval area #5)

Evidence:
- `extract/specs.md:240-242` - the entire required a11y section is *"WCAG level: [AA or AAA]"* plus *"[Any specific accessibility requirements]"* - a freeform blank.
- `extract/library.md:320` / `contract/README.md:35` - the contract's a11y field is a single freeform string: `a11y: "[role, aria attributes, keyboard behaviour]"`. No structured requirement for keyboard operability, focus management, form-control association, or reduced-motion.
- Grep confirms `reduced-motion` / `prefers-reduced-motion` / `form-association` = **0 hits** in `extract/` + `_shared/`, even though motion tokens exist (`common.css` `--zimm-motion-*`). Path D (`extract/specs.md:151`) mentions a11y only as optional "intent" notes.
- `validate.mjs` performs no a11y check of any kind.

Process gap: WCAG AA is declared in config but never decomposed into required, checkable spec content. A11y is an afterthought the agent can leave blank and still pass every gate.

Downstream symptom: 26 draft specs with unstructured a11y strings and no reduced-motion story for an animated retail site - AA is aspirational, not verified.

Fix: Replace the freeform a11y section in `extract/specs.md` and the contract with a required checklist keyed to WCAG AA: keyboard operation, visible focus + focus order, ARIA roles/states, form label association, target size, and `prefers-reduced-motion` handling for any component using motion tokens. Add an a11y-completeness check to `validate.mjs` and the handover gate.

---

## Finding 8 - Token strategy is a static px scale only, with no fluid/breakpoint token layer and no guard against tokens.md ↔ common.css drift.
**Severity: Medium-High** (directly answers eval area #3)

Evidence:
- `extract/library.md:68-77` (Mode A category table) enumerates only static categories; "Grid / breakpoints" is captured *only if* the Figma source happens to expose "named breakpoint values." There is no instruction to synthesise a fluid type ramp or breakpoint token set.
- `extract/library.md:104-110` - first-extraction writes values 1:1 with no fluid strategy; naming is `--[prefix]-[category]-[name]` with no size-per-breakpoint concept.
- Drift: the only safeguard is the behavioural note `extract/library.md:43-46` ("Output discipline... capture every real change"). No validator compares `tokens.md` against `common.css`. Verified symptom: `common.css` type scale is entirely px (`--zimm-font-size-*`, `--zimm-font-lineheight-*`), letter-spacing in px, and the drift already shows (`#969696` hardcoded where a grey token exists).

Process gap: Tokens are extracted as a flat static snapshot. Fluid/responsive typography and breakpoint tokens are never part of the schema, and nothing verifies the doc and the CSS agree.

Fix: Add a fluid-token strategy to `library.md` Step 1b/1c: base `rem`, `clamp()`-based type/space ramps, and a first-class breakpoint token group derived from Figma layout grids. Add a `validate.mjs` (or dedicated) check that every token in `tokens.md` exists in `common.css` with a matching value, and vice versa.

---

## Finding 9 - Component spec co-production is declared mandatory ("always") but is unenforced and structurally hidden from the handover index.
**Severity: Medium** (compounds Finding 2; answers eval area #6)

Evidence:
- `extract/library.md:349` - *"This step is always run alongside component extraction. The spec and the library element are co-produced. They are not optional relative to each other."*
- Yet nothing verifies it, and `index-generator.md:34` explicitly excludes `02-design/specs/components/` from the scan.
- Verified symptom: 27 contract components, 16 component spec files - 11 "always-produced" specs never got produced, and the handover index cannot see the gap.

Process gap: An "always" instruction with no post-condition check and a reporting layer that doesn't look where the artifact lives. The strongest wording in the pipeline is silently violable.

Fix: Fold a "every contract component has a spec at `02-design/specs/components/[name].md`" assertion into the Finding-2 handover gate and into `validate.mjs`. Have `index-generator.md` reconcile the contract against the components spec folder and list any component whose spec is missing rather than skipping the folder.

---

## Cross-cutting note
The unifying defect is that **every quality rule in this pipeline is phrased as agent guidance, and almost none is a gate.** `validate.mjs` is the only executable check, and it validates atomic-model integrity only - a narrow slice presented (in `README.md:70-78` and `authoring.md:120-125`) as "definition of done." Everything the engineers flagged (px, direction, monolithic styles, weak provenance) corresponds to a rule that either does not exist (Findings 1, 3, 5) or exists only as prose the agent can pass over (Findings 4, 6, 7, 9). The highest-leverage remediation is to convert the readiness moment (`handover/SKILL.md` + `index-generator.md` Step 4) from an unverified question into an executable gate, and to broaden `validate.mjs` from atomic-model-only to a real coverage/fidelity/a11y/hardcoded-value check.
